notes: No AI provider publishes per-request figures for Claude. These factors are grounded in current (2026) peer-reviewed and industry measurements of LLM inference energy, carry an uncertainty band shown in the UI, and are revised continually. Token counts for Claude Code are EXACT (read from local session transcripts), so on that path the only remaining uncertainty is these energy factors. Data vintage: 2026.

sources.note: 2026 measurements: optimised frontier inference median ~0.31 Wh/query (IQR 0.16-0.60); per output token ~0.0001-0.002 Wh spanning small to large models. GPT-4o-class ~0.3 Wh for a 500-token window. Decode (output) is >=96% of energy for typical generation. Sources: ScienceDirect S2542435126001145; TokenPowerBench (AAAI 2026); arXiv 2507.11417.

Prefill (input) is <=3.4% of inference energy for standard generation vs >=96% for decode, so per-token input energy is roughly 0.03-0.05x an output token; rises for very long contexts due to quadratic attention. Source: arXiv 2512.22066.

Cache reads skip prefill recompute but still incur KV-cache memory bandwidth during decode, so ~0.1x fresh-input energy (also Anthropic's cache-read price ratio). Measured on real Claude Code sessions: 93-94% of input tokens are cache reads. Transcripts give the exact fresh/cache split per message.

Energy per token scales ~with active parameters (Anthropic does not publish these). Tiers span the measured 0.0001-0.002 Wh/token range relative to a Sonnet-class baseline (1.0). To be replaced with measured figures from ML.ENERGY and Hugging Face AI Energy Score.

US regional grid ~321 gCO2e/kWh (IEA-derived, 2026); the US hosts ~45% of AI datacentre capacity and Claude runs primarily in US regions, so US intensity is used rather than the ~396 gCO2e/kWh global average. Will become datacentre-region-aware.

Onsite cooling water use effectiveness ~1.1 L/kWh (Google best-in-class fleet; hyperscaler-disclosed range ~0.2-1.8; liquid cooling cuts onsite use 70-90%). This alone gives ~0.26-0.32 mL for a short query (Gemini/ChatGPT scope-1 figures).

Offsite water to GENERATE the electricity, which is comparable to or larger than onsite cooling. US thermoelectric consumptive average ~1.25 L/kWh (EIA); we use consumptive (evaporated) not withdrawal, the honest metric. Grid-mix and region dependent; LBNL cites up to 7.6 L/kWh for dirtier grids. Including offsite raises per-query water 5-20x over onsite alone.
